newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S AAPT PLANS A$305 MLN INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S AAPT PLANS A$305 MLN INVESTMENT.

text.p: Australian telecommunications group AAPT Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to invest A$305 million over the next five years as part of its strategic plan.
AAPT said it planned to spend most of this investment with local industry.

"AAPT will also consider collaborative development projects with specialised research bodies in Australia and with Australian and overseas companies with expertise relevant to our business growth plans," AAPT director Trevor Harris said.

"We have already taken a number of steps to faciliate access by Australian abd Australian-based businesses to key export markets of Asia, North America, the Middle East and Europe," Harris said in a statement.
AAPT said it planned to increase the number of employees to about 1,200 over the next five years from 600 currently.
AAPT has spent A$100 million on its local infrastructure over the past six years.

AAPT is 51 percent owned by AAP Information Services, which also owns Australian Associated Press, Australia's national news agency. Major shareholders in AAPIS are John Fairfax Holdings Ltd and News Corp Ltd.
Singapore Telecommunications Ltd and the unlisted Todd Corp of New Zealand are the minority shareholders with 24.5 percent each.
Australia's telecommunications industry was fully deregulated on July 1.
